races.name: Ladbrokes 'Bet £5 Get £30 New Customer Offer' EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's stablemate is absent here but Connor Beasley partners this consistent hold-up type who has posted 3 placings from 15 runs on similar good ground and goes well fresh on a 10-day return; genuine closer who needs a true gallop to get involved.|

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran partnered by apprentice Amie Waugh (3lb claim) returning after 21 days; races from off the pace and has been struggling in form with recent finishes of 13th, 6th and 8th, and 0 wins from 15 on comparable ground raises stamina-for-pace concerns.|

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field and the pivotal horse in the pace map; Mark Winn takes the ride for Jim Goldie and the horse steps up from 5f where most of his recent form has been built, making the extra furlong a mild query, though the uncontested lead on quick ground compensates.|

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by W H Harrison (quiet 14-day record of 0/2) who brings strong 5f form including back-to-back runner-up finishes; moving to 6f and good-to-firm ground at Ayr, his natural hold-up style means he depends on Water Of Leith setting a pace that stretches the field.|

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground earlier this season, which is the standout form line here; a true hold-up horse by nature, the redistribution means she is unlikely to get a forward position even if her jockey attempts it, so her chance hinges on getting a clean run from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner returning on a 21-day break with poor recent form (12th, 8th, 17th) and a style fit flag indicating she would not naturally race from the midfield position shown; her best efforts came over 5f and the hold-up pattern over 6f on this ground looks tough.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly fitted with a hood; races from hold-up but her form figures (6,9,8,4,4) on similar surfaces show no win from 6 runs on comparable going and no place at all, with the style fit flag adding a further caution against expecting her to travel powerfully from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes over on this Jim Goldie 4-year-old whose recent form string includes long-distance efforts over 7f-10f — the drop back to 6f is a significant trip reduction, and as a genuine hold-up type pushed forward on the map, she is the horse least likely to fulfil any prominent role.|

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won over 6f on standard going and placed over 6f on good-to-soft, giving her the most relevant recent form of the true hold-up brigade; James Sullivan (experienced claimer) partners for R Mike Smith and she arrives on a short 7-day turnaround, but she is a natural closer who needs the race to set up late.|

races.paceDynamic: Water Of Leith is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Ayr, and with no natural rival to pressure him, he is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, uncontested clip. The remainder of the field — Mr Cool, Kelpie Grey, Great Profit, Cotai Starlight, Joshuas Dream, Falcon Queen, Tap Dancer, and Lanarra — are all hold-up or midfield types by nature, meaning the early pace is entirely in Water Of Leith's hands. Several runners tagged as redistributed (Cotai Starlight, Joshuas Dream, Falcon Queen, Tap Dancer, Lanarra) are true hold-up horses pushed forward on the map only because the field is so hold-up heavy that they cannot all take their natural position; the pace shape will still resolve to one leader and a wall of chasers. This race shape strongly favours a well-judged front-runner who dictates a fair but not scorching gallop, and any hold-up horse that can produce a genuine sustained finish from the two-furlong pole, rather than a single burst of speed, has the best chance of pegging Water Of Leith back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leith Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith jumps well and dictates an honest but not frantic pace, allowing him to conserve enough to repel challengers.
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith sets the fractions exactly as he likes with no rival willing to take him on, giving his rider full control of the race tempo; on good-to-firm ground over 6f at Ayr, a well-rated front-runner rolling from the front without pressure is notoriously hard to catch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith's early pace is just quick enough to stretch the field but leaves him vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses who travel best through the race and produce the most sustained finishing effort will arrive late as Leith's advantage narrows; Ayr's fair track does not unduly penalise those coming from off the pace in a truly run 6f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-leaning types successfully pushes forward early to sit close to Water Of Leith and benefits from a position just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A horse that tracks the leader at close range conserves energy through the race without doing the donkey work, emerging as the freshest challenger at the two-furlong pole; on fast ground, this stalking position over 6f can be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith is challenged unexpectedly early, inflating the gallop and draining the whole field, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace would compress finishing positions and hand an advantage to whichever hold-up horse encounters the cleanest passage and covers ground most efficiently; this scenario is low probability given the field's uniformly hold-up profile and lack of a genuine pace challenger.

watchPoints.text: Water Of Leith's jumping and early position is the single most important moment of this race — if he breaks smartly and crosses to the rail unchallenged, the race shape is set; watch whether any unexpected rival follows him forward to inject pace.|

Tap Dancer's trip drop from 7f-10f to 6f is severe — if Paul Mulrennan tries to push her forward to offset the hold-up congestion, she could set an artificially strong pace that scrambles the entire race shape.|

Cotai Starlight, Joshuas Dream and Falcon Queen are all natural rear-runners likely to be fighting for the same ground in the closing stages; traffic and cover problems for this group at the two-furlong pole could be a key race-deciding factor.|

The going is confirmed good-to-firm for this race despite the card header showing Good — horses with form on fast ground (Cotai Starlight's 6f win on good, Lanarra's 6f win on standard) gain a small profile boost over those whose best form came on soft.|

Jim Goldie saddles four runners (Water Of Leith, Kelpie Grey, Joshuas Dream, Tap Dancer) — watch market moves closer to post time for any stable indication, and note that split-stable tactics could inadvertently shape the race if more than one of his horses is ridden aggressively early.|

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forbidden Colours
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old trained by Ed Walker with Kieran Shoemark aboard, carrying 130lbs off OR 71; in this race she will settle further back than her midfield mapping implies, as she is a natural hold-up horse, and the restrained pace makes a winning late run harder to produce.|

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter here for Katie Scott, Jason Hart up; placed twice on Good ground over this trip and distance range, she gets to dictate entirely unchallenged from the front and that uncontested role is her single biggest asset in this race.|

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has genuine course-and-distance winning form on Good ground and boasts a strong recent record of three wins from fifteen similar-going starts; Paul Mulrennan rides and, as a true hold-up type, she needs enough pace ahead of her to produce her best — a moderate tempo is her main risk.|

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's five-year-old has won his last two and carries top weight of 138lbs, but Connor Beasley will have to settle him further off the pace than he would ideally like — his natural role is closer to prominent — and the steady tempo slightly compromises the full effect of his recent winning momentum.|

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: A six-year-old in fine form for Michael Dods with two wins from his last five, wearing a hood and set to race prominently; only three days since his last run is worth noting, but he is clearly trained fresh and will be the key pressure agent on Carmel Valley through the early part of the race.|

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's consistent eight-year-old has strung together three consecutive thirds on Good ground over 6-7f; Jake Dickson claims 5lb off 140lbs, but as a hold-up horse, Abduction is most vulnerable in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to pull the field apart for a closing finish.|

races.paceDynamic: Carmel Valley is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field over 7f on Good to Firm ground at Ayr, and with no rival capable of matching her early, she sets a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Roaring Ralph will push forward from a prominent position and apply some pressure through the early stages, but the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, leaving Carmel Valley able to dictate rhythm and conserve energy into the straight. Forbidden Colours and Imperial Guard are genuine hold-up operators redistributed into the midfield graphic because the map cannot accommodate all rear-runners; they will sit further back than shown, meaning the closing thrust depends on a strong enough tempo being set — which, with only one confirmed pace-setter, is not guaranteed. This race shape strongly favours prominent and pace-pressing runners who can travel smoothly behind a controlled gallop and kick decisively in the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who need a truly run race to generate a late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Carmel Valley Controls, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Carmel Valley dictates a measured gallop and prominent raiders track her into the straight before unleashing their finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Carmel Valley sets a comfortable rhythm and Roaring Ralph stalks her closely throughout, with the pair pulling clear of those held up further back; on Good to Firm ground over 7f, horses that travel in the first two or three are best placed to quicken when the race begins in earnest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injected, Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph pushes hard at Carmel Valley early and the tempo genuinely increases, stretching the field and opening the race up for closers.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace draws the stamina reserves of front and prominent runners and the hold-up horses get the strong gallop they need to produce their best late runs; Native Honey and Imperial Guard, who both carry winning form on this trip and going, would be prime beneficiaries from behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Carmel Valley is completely uncontested and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Running her own race at a comfortable tempo on fast ground, Carmel Valley saves enough energy to sprint clear in the final furlong before rivals can rally; with a small, unthreatening field, a wide-margin front-running success is a genuine, if minority, outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the held-up horses sprint from the back of the field to catch a flat-out Carmel Valley.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Forbidden Colours and Imperial Guard — both redistributed away from their true rear position — getting the run of the race late and finding enough clear ground in a small field; the STYLE_FIT discounts mean their chances in this shape are materially reduced, making this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Roaring Ralph is the key pace pressure point — watch whether he pushes hard at Carmel Valley early or settles behind her, as this single factor determines whether the race is truly truly run or becomes a slow-tempo exercise in the straight.

Native Honey's hold-up role makes her reliant on the gallop being strong enough to sustain a run from off the pace; if the tempo is moderate, watch how far back Paul Mulrennan elects to settle her through the early stages.

Imperial Guard's STYLE_FIT tag means he is racing somewhat out of role in this shape — watch whether Connor Beasley tries to creep closer than expected in running, which could signal a bid to offset the unfavourable race shape.

With only 6 runners, field positioning in the first two furlongs will be clearly visible — watch for any early crowding that disrupts Roaring Ralph's bid to secure second spot behind Carmel Valley, as that could alter the entire shape of the race.

Abduction's jockey Jake Dickson claims 5lb on a horse already placed in similar conditions; watch whether the combination sits closer to the pace than form suggests, as a small field sometimes compresses running styles.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get More With Ladbucks' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's mare has been campaigned at longer trips on Good and Standard recently and drops back to a mile here; her instinct is to come from well off the pace, which is the most difficult position to play in this shape — the 67-day absence adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Returns after a 321-day layoff for Jim Goldie, which is the headline concern — even a straightforward return to form on Good ground (where she has placed) cannot be assumed after nearly a year off, and her natural hold-up style compounds the tactical difficulty.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has won twice on Good ground over a mile in recent starts and arrives fresh off a 22-day break; her natural instinct is to come from off the pace, and while that style is congested in this field, her superior good-ground form makes her the most interesting of the genuine closers.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago and won over nine furlongs on Good ground, showing he stays well; his true preference is to be held up, and in a race where the rear is overcrowded, his 140lb burden and apprentice jockey Tom Kiely-Marshall add to the challenge of finding a clear run.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up specialist who has been running over shorter trips on softer ground of late; his sim-going record on Good is thin, he arrives after a 38-day absence, and the stiff 140lb weight makes it hard to see him getting competitive unless the pace scenario plays perfectly into his hands.

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter who should get a clean lead and dictate terms; recent form shows consecutive out-of-the-frame finishes but those came in more competitive contexts, and the visor is retained — his value here is entirely positional rather than on bare form.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on Good ground in recent form and ran well just seven days ago — the key angle here is that he can travel prominently enough to exploit Keats House's moderate pace, with Jason Hart's positive ride style a significant asset in this tactical race.

runners_data.name: Eeetee
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has returned a string of below-par finishing positions on all surfaces recently, and his Good-ground sim record is poor; despite occasionally being noted as prominent-going, the form figures offer little encouragement in a field with several more credible contenders.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's charge has placed on Good ground over this distance and Connor Beasley can place him handily; his consistent record of making the frame suggests he travels well enough to sit close to the pace and pick up late — a natural beneficiary of the dominant scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Keats House is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, he should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop around Ayr's flat mile. The pace is unlikely to be searching — a lone leader bowling along on Good to Firm ground at his own rhythm creates a genuinely attritional shape where the race may not truly ignite until the final two furlongs. This race shape most favours hold-up horses with a late turn of foot, provided they can make up ground on a track that can be unforgiving if the pace collapses too late. However, the field is stacked with natural hold-up types — Novak, Mayor Of Maghera, Samra Star, Spirit Of Nature, Approaching Dawn and others all want to come from off the pace — meaning the rear will be crowded and only those positioned closest to the leader at halfway will avoid being caught flat-footed; Runninsonofagun and Union Island, who have shown the ability to travel prominently when needed, are best placed to exploit the moderate pace with a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keats House Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House gets a clean break and no rival challenges for the lead, setting a gentle, uncontested tempo.
scenarios.body: Keats House controls every yard, lobbing along on Good to Firm ground before kicking for home entering the final quarter-mile; horses tracking him closely throughout gain the decisive positional advantage when the race quickens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Keats House within a length or two throughout and produces the stronger finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop suits a horse travelling just off the pace in second or third, poised to hit the front approaching the final furlong without having to make ground from deep; Runninsonofagun and Union Island have the form and positional flexibility to execute this profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up sharply from two furlongs out, creating enough of a gap for a genuine closer to weave through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Approaching Dawn has the most compelling form on similar going and has proven she can finish strongly over this trip; the scenario demands a true injection of pace mid-race and a clear passage, both of which are uncertain given how crowded the rear will be with natural hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so slow that the entire field compresses into a heap turning for home, producing a rough and chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses unable to get their natural position, the race could degenerate into a bunched cavalry charge where any midfield runner could stumble into a placing; Novak and Union Island have the tactical speed to benefit from a sprint, though this shape is the hardest to predict.

watchPoints.text: Keats House's early break is critical — if he stumbles or is caught wide exiting the stalls, the entire race shape collapses and the field will have no pace to aim at.

The rear of the field will be dangerously congested with natural hold-up types — watch for Approaching Dawn, Mayor Of Maghera and Novak all competing for the same ground from the four-furlong pole, increasing the risk of trouble in running for any of them.
Spirit Of Nature returns after 321 days off — if she tires and weakens in the straight, she could cause interference for the closers attempting to thread through; flag her position throughout.

Runninsonofagun ran just seven days ago — monitor in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of flatness, as a below-par show from him removes the most likely prominent challenger to Keats House and opens the race up further.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race, replacing the advertised Good — horses with winning or placed form specifically on Good to Firm (Keats House, Approaching Dawn) receive a quiet upgrade in conditions suitability.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rastnet
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with Beasley booked; five consecutive placed efforts suggest reliability rather than a winning edge, but her role shaping this race is decisive — similar-going record reads just one win from nine attempts, so she may be vulnerable when challenged.|

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: O'Meara runner with strong similar-going form (2W7P from 15 starts) returning after just 18 days; hg:h tag suggests held-up tendencies that may conflict with a prominent map position, and eight career starts at 10f offer solid distance credentials.|

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Goldie's 6-year-old arrives on the back of a win 14 days ago (1/10f/GOO) and boasts excellent similar-going form (12/15); a confirmed hold-up performer perfectly suited to the race shape Rastnet is expected to create.|

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: The 3-year-old from Crisford's yard won over 10f on good ground and has shown he can race prominently; a 45-day absence is the key question mark, though the yard's 3/16 recent strike rate is modest.|

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's second string, with an excellent similar-going record (14/15) and consistent placings at shorter trips — stepping up in trip to 1m2f is the variable, but his hold-up style suits this pace map and Mullen rides him regularly.|

runners_data.name: Empirical
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3-year-old won on good ground over 8f most recently; a natural prominent racer by inclination, his placement in midfield reflects a crowded position market — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and his chance depends heavily on whether he can recover a forward berth.|

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Goldie's 8-year-old has won three of his last five starts over 11-12f on good ground and is clearly in form, but his front-running tendencies are being suppressed by Rastnet's presence — forced to race off the pace, his chance is materially compromised compared to when he can lead.

races.paceDynamic: Rastnet is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no credible challenger likely to dispute the lead over 1m2f on good-to-firm ground, Connor Beasley should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. Colourband and Obito will press from prominent positions but neither is a natural front-runner, meaning Rastnet should settle comfortably on the bridle through the middle portion of the race without being harried into a pace that would burn her out. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate — Empirical and Alpine Sierra are genuine front-runners by inclination but are shown in midfield because Rastnet figures to secure the rail and the early lead ahead of them, leaving those two racing out of their preferred roles. This race shape — a single uncontested pacer setting an honest but not extreme gallop on fast ground over a flat mile-and-a-quarter — strongly favours hold-up horses who can track the tempo and produce a sustained late run, with Pearl Eye and Geo the most obvious beneficiaries of a well-regulated contest that plays into the hands of closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rastnet Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rastnet bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest enough to string the field out, enabling the hold-up horses to pick off the leader in the straight.
scenarios.body: Rastnet sets a comfortable rhythm and the race only truly ignites in the final 2f, where horses with proven stamina at this trip and beyond come into their own.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Rastnet sets only a modest crawl and the field bunches up, robbing the closers of the run-in they need to reel her back.
scenarios.body: Beasley conserves energy through a slow early pace and kicks off the home bend, leaving hold-up horses too much to do in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Colourband or Obito exert more pressure on Rastnet than expected, creating a contested pace that burns out the leader but is still fast enough to favour prominent racers over closers.
scenarios.body: A pressured Rastnet fades but the race is won in the straight by a horse who was always travelling just behind the pace rather than deep in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Upset Result
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly dawdling early and Empirical or Alpine Sierra — despite being pushed out of their natural prominent positions — manage to recover and find a prominent berth.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their preferred roles, these horses carry style-fit discounts and only threaten if the race devolves into a tactical scramble where position off the turn becomes decisive.

watchPoints.text: Pearl Eye — if Rastnet delivers an honest gallop, Mulrennan will have Pearl Eye travelling ominously in rear and she arrives with a recent course-and-distance-equivalent win in identical conditions; the chief danger to the race outcome.

Alpine Sierra — watch whether Lauren Young (5) attempts to push Alpine Sierra forward regardless of Rastnet; if these two clash for the lead, the pace dynamic changes significantly and hold-up horses benefit even more.

Empirical — Kieran Shoemark is experienced enough to try to find a prominent position for a horse that wants to be there; if he slots in second or third early, his style-fit discount lessens and he becomes more competitive than the map suggests.

Colourband — Jason Hart will look to use the likely early pace set by Rastnet as a reference point, and after 45 days off the Crisford runner needs to find his rhythm quickly over this trip; the first furlong will reveal whether he is fit enough to travel prominently.

Geo — Mullen has consistently ridden this horse and knows his needs; watch for a patient ride from the back, with the quality of Rastnet's pace being the critical factor in whether Geo can close sufficiently on a flat track.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for John Wainwright and Jason Hart, showing consistent placed form at 5f on good ground; posted four placed efforts from five similar-going runs and is the most straightforward late finisher in the field if the pace fires them in.

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Linda Perratt and Connor Beasley who stays honest in hold-up races on good ground; his one win from 15 similar-going runs comes at 5f and his recent third at Ayr on comparable conditions keeps him squarely in contention.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and pace anchor for this race; rated 0.93 style fit for this prominent role at Ayr, she carries a headgear flag, goes for Jim Goldie who is 4/40 over the last 14 days, and her 10/15 runs on good-type ground with a win included make her the key tactical reference point throughout.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner for Iain Jardine and Andrew Mullen returning after 35 days; her most recent win was over this exact 5f trip on good ground and she holds the highest similar-going win ratio (1W from only 5 runs), making her a serious player if she handles the return from a break well.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old with a visor flag and excellent 10/15 record on good-type ground including a win at 6f; Paul Mulrennan rides a horse whose natural prominent style suits tracking Wee Mary closely, and his most recent victory was over 6f on good ground just 11 days ago — he is the most naturally positioned closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's five-year-old who arrives after just seven days; his hold-up style means he is carried forward on the pace map because the field's back-end is over-subscribed, and his modest recent form (637756) at 6f on good ground means his redistribution is context rather than a form plus.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for R Mike Smith, ridden by claimer Amie Waugh (3lb), whose most recent run produced a clear 2nd over 6f on good going 16 days ago; genuinely hold-up in style but squeezed into a midfield position on the map by the weight of hold-up types — her 0W1P from 10 similar-going runs limits expectation regardless of scenario.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old, last seen seven days ago, whose recent form is built around 6f and 7f rather than today's sharp 5f trip; she holds up naturally but is mapped to midfield due to field congestion, and the step back in trip to 5f on fast ground is an untested variable that represents a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's eight-year-old ridden by five-pound claimer Tom Kiely-Marshall and fitted with a hood; his record of 0W4P from 10 similar-going runs at 5f underlines a consistent but limited ceiling, and though he fills midfield on the map, his true rearward preference means he will need the pace to collapse for his effort to land.

races.paceDynamic: Wee Mary is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-horse field over Ayr's sharp 5f on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to control tempo from the off at a pace entirely of her choosing — sustainable and metronomic rather than suicidal. Behind her, Doon The Glen is the most likely horse to press or track prominently, while Startling, Henery Hawk, Supremissy, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Summerstorms Dream and Sixcor all have hold-up tendencies that crowd the rear of the field. This race shape — a lone leader dictating a fair but uncontested gallop over a short track — strongly favours those who can race in close pursuit of the pace and produce a decisive kick in the final furlong, making prominent-to-midfield closers the primary beneficiaries. The field carries significantly more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear in a nine-runner 5f sprint, and Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Summerstorms Dream and Sixcor are the runners most likely to find themselves pushed forward out of their natural position and unable to replicate their preferred late style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wee Mary Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary is allowed to roll along in front uncontested and sets a fair but not excessive gallop, rewarding the horse that tracks her most closely.
scenarios.body: Wee Mary dictates every yard at a rhythm that keeps her rivals honest but never stretched, and a prominent tracker who can quicken off the pace in the final furlong will sweep past as the gap narrows. Doon The Glen is ideally placed to hunt her down, while Supremissy's recent form suggests enough finishing speed to make this shape pay.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected — perhaps from Doon The Glen pushing forward to pressure Wee Mary — and the front end burns out inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace on quick ground over 5f can leave leaders vulnerable, and a hold-up runner who has conserved energy through the first half can pick up the pieces. Henery Hawk and Startling both carry decent recent form on similar going and would be the most credible closers if this scenario materialises, though genuine hold-up types are crowded in this field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wee Mary Front-Runs All the Way
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly uncontested and Wee Mary sets a leisurely enough gallop that she retains enough in reserve to repel challengers in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: On a sharp track with no rival willing to go with her, Wee Mary could control the pace so completely that she steals a march and holds on under Mark Winn, who rides her for a yard trainer in Jim Goldie. The headgear flag and her 10/15 runs on similar going underline this as a live possibility if the field misjudges how much she has banked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If positional chaos at the break reshuffles the pack and a runner otherwise expected to be outpaced gets a tow into proceedings earlier than anticipated.
scenarios.body: Short-priced logic breaks down when unexpectedly compressed early running order levels the playing field, and a horse like Sixcor or Ski Angel — who regularly posts placed efforts at this course and trip on comparable going — could benefit from the muddled shape. These are low-probability outcomes precisely because neither is a true natural hold-up horse despite their map position, and the redistribution context caps the ceiling here.

watchPoints.text: Wee Mary's unchallenged lead — if Mark Winn gets her into an uncontested rhythm inside the first furlong, the entire race shape pivots around whether any prominent tracker can close the gap late; watch the first 100 yards for any sign she is being hunted.

Doon The Glen's early positioning — Paul Mulrennan must commit promptly to track Wee Mary from a prominent berth; any hesitation in a nine-runner 5f sprint on fast ground and the gap will be too large to bridge in the closing stages.

Summerstorms Dream's trip drop — she has not raced over 5f in recent form and all her historical placed efforts are at 6f or beyond; watch how she travels through the early pace, as a horse who finds 5f too sharp could block or impede runners around her.

Claimer impact — both Ski Angel (Amie Waugh, 3lb) and Sixcor (Tom Kiely-Marshall, 5lb) carry apprentice allowances that could theoretically compress the weights meaningfully; watch whether either rider is able to position their horse closer than their natural style would suggest at the start.

Supremissy's return from 35 days — her trainer Iain Jardine is 3/20 over the last 14 days and the gelding returns fresh; horses who win fresh for this yard at 5f on fast ground are worth monitoring for early market moves that might confirm she has been prepared for this.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with a clear positional advantage on today's flat Ayr track; the OR=60 mark and recent 1st at 10f on Good give it solid credentials, though stepping up to 1m2f from shorter distances and the tp headgear are worth noting — the slow pace it creates flatters its own chance most.|

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners a genuine hold-up mare for Jim Goldie, who has four winners from 40 runners over the past fortnight; her recent form at 8f-10f on Good is modest (best of 4th) and the step to 1m2f is a question mark, but she is well weighted at OR=60.|

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Lauren Young (5lb claim) pairs up with a stayer who has three consecutive 3rds over 13f on Good — the drop back to 1m2f may actually sharpen her finishing effort; Goldie's in-form stable and a prominent style that suits today's shape make this a well-positioned runner.|

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen rides a hold-up specialist who has competed almost exclusively at 16f+ over Good ground, making the 1m2f trip a significant drop in distance; the blindfold headgear is noted, and while stamina is obvious his ability to produce a quick finish over this shorter trip is unproven.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's gelding ran just seven days ago and recorded a 2nd at 10f on Good, making it the freshest form in the field at this trip; a prominent racing style with blinkers suits the likely slow-pace scenario and Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking at this level.|

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Tom Kiely-Marshall takes the 5lb claim on an 8-year-old whose entire recent history is over 12f-16f on Good — the trip is almost certainly short of her best, and while the form line shows a 4th last time, the distance profile is a material concern today.|

runners_data.name: Betty Bassett
runners_data.note: 42 days off the track for Christopher Kellett, whose yard is 0 from 3 over the past fortnight; all five historical runs listed are at 8f, making this 1m2f trip a career-first attempt at the distance, and blinkers are fitted — fitness and suitability are both questions.|

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 5-year-old recorded a win at 10f on Good most recently and her form over 10f-12f on similar ground reads 1-2-3-5; she is a natural hold-up runner whose true style places her at the back of the field — the race is only likely to fall her way if the pace is genuine rather than the slow gallop Royal Blaze seems set to dictate.|

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a horse that won last time at 8f on Good and has a 1-3 in its last two, but whose hold-up style means it was mapped into midfield rather than its natural rearward position; Christopher Kellett's trainer record of 0 from 3 recently tempers enthusiasm, and the hold-up approach is a tactical handicap here.|

runners_data.name: Lightning Galaxy
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a 4-year-old wearing a hood whose last five runs show a string of 9s and 10s in finishes — form figures of 0-9-9-5-9 paint a bleak picture; a natural hold-up runner with no recent win at any trip on Good ground, placed in midfield only because the field is heavy with backmarkers.|

runners_data.name: One More Bottle
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh takes over on a 5-year-old returning from a 198-day layoff — the longest absence in this field by a wide margin; all recent form is on Standard (AW) and a return to turf after a lengthy break makes reliability difficult to assess, with the hold-up style further disadvantaged by today's likely slow pace.|

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old last ran seven days ago (6th at 10f, Good) for trainer R Mike Smith, whose yard has two winners from 15 over 14 days; a hold-up operator on a big field card, Golden Valour's proximity to today's track profile is mildly encouraging, but age and a consistent pattern of mid-to-rear finishes limit the upside.|

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: Shay Farmer (5lb) partners the lowest-rated runner in the field (OR=45) for R Mike Smith; form of 0-9-5-4-9 offers little encouragement, the 10f Good history is the nearest comparable to today's conditions, and a natural backmarker style leaves this horse entirely dependent on a strongly-run race that the pace map does not promise.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Blaze is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to push it through the early stages, is set to dictate an unhurried gallop over this 1m2f Good to Firm Ayr track. Falcon Nine and Annandale will press forward to prominent positions, but with Royal Blaze uncontested at the head of affairs the tempo is likely to be controlled and moderate, compressing the field into a tactical contest. The going report confirms Good to Firm throughout the card, which rewards horses with a sustained cruising speed rather than those relying on a deep-seated closing kick off a truly run race. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and front-runners who can sit just off a sedate pace, conserve energy through the middle sections, and have enough to resist a challenge in the final two furlongs — hold-up horses that need a proper gallop to land blows are disadvantaged. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Recobella, Daring Leader, Lightning Galaxy, One More Bottle, Golden Valour, and Zebra Star are all true hold-up horses shuffled into a midfield representation, but the most likely to secure anything close to a forward position are Recobella and Daring Leader given their recent winning form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Blaze bowls along unchallenged and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that suits those racing just behind it.
scenarios.body: Royal Blaze dictates the fractions from the front, with Falcon Nine and Annandale tucking in close and travelling well on good to firm ground; the race turns into a sustained-speed contest in the final quarter-mile where those with a prominent pitch have a decisive positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Falcon Nine and Annandale both press Royal Blaze from early, applying just enough pressure to expose its limitations in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger gallop than Scenario A develops as two horses track the leader closely, meaning Royal Blaze is vulnerable if it has given its all by the two-furlong pole; Falcon Nine's recent 2nd at 10f on Good and Annandale's course-appropriate stamina at 11f-13f give both a genuine claims to collar the leader late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up runner finds a gap to finish fast.
scenarios.body: Recobella or Daring Leader, both recent winners on Good ground at 10f-12f, would need the tempo to be genuinely honest rather than falsely steady; given the likely sedate nature of Royal Blaze's pace this is a less probable scenario, though Recobella's 1W form at today's trip is the strongest closing case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Wide Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Blaze is headed before halfway or the pace collapses entirely, causing a bunched, unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: A breakdown in the race shape would randomise the outcome and reduce positional advantage to near-zero; Penelope's Sister and Ravenscraig Castle, both patient types with stamina credentials, could benefit from the ensuing scramble.

watchPoints.text: Royal Blaze controls the tempo from the front without a serious rival — watch whether Falcon Nine has the early speed to apply pressure before the home turn, as that single dynamic will determine whether the race produces a genuine test or a sprint-finish from a crawl.

Falcon Nine ran just seven days ago and carries blinkers — monitor whether any residual fatigue from that quick turnaround shows in the early furlongs, as Kieran Shoemark may be forced to use him more prominently than ideal if the early pace is very slow.

Recobella and Daring Leader are both true hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map — watch how Jason Hart and Jake Dickson navigate the early stages, because if the pace is as slow as projected neither will generate the momentum required to finish through the field.

Annandale's last five runs are all at 11f-13f on Good — the drop to 1m2f today is shorter than anything in her recent history, so watch whether Lauren Young elects to push forward early and use that positional advantage rather than waiting for a stamina test that may not materialise.

Betty Bassett and One More Bottle are both significant risks for non-completion or early detachment — the former makes a debut at this trip after 42 days off, the latter returns from 198 days away; both are worth tracking in running for signs of distress that could disrupt the pack.
